title: Basic Auction Formats
body_html:
Basic Auction Formats

The basic auction layer specialises the generic MechanismWithTransfers ([[mechanism_design.transfer.mechanisms_with_transfers]]) interface to two classical auction shapes: single-item auctions and multi-item auctions.

Single-item auction

SingleItemAuction I V P extends MechanismWithTransfers I (fun _ => V) (Option I) P with no extra data. The components are:

  • Bidders: a finite (typically) index type I.
  • Bids: each bidder reports a scalar value in V.
  • Allocation: the outcome type is Option I —
  • some i means bidder i receives the single item;
  • none means the item is withheld (e.g. the reserve price was not met).
  • Payments: per-bidder transfers in P.

Importantly, the structure does not commit to which bidder wins. The specific allocation rule (highest bidder, weighted scoring, randomised allocation, …) is supplied by each concrete instantiation — see [[mechanism_design.auction.basic.second_price_mechanism]] and [[mechanism_design.auction.basic.first_price_mechanism]].

Multi-item auction

MultiItemAuction I k V P extends MechanismWithTransfers I (fun _ => Fin k → V) (I → Finset (Fin k)) P:

  • Bids: each bidder submits a value vector $b_i : \mathrm{Fin}\,k \to V$, one bid per item type.
  • Allocation: a function $a : I \to \mathrm{Finset}\,(\mathrm{Fin}\,k)$ assigning a bundle of items to each bidder.

The structure imposes no feasibility constraint by default; the companion predicate MultiItemAuction.IsFeasible records the no-double-allocation requirement: $$ \forall i \ne j.\; \mathrm{allocationRule}(b, i) \cap \mathrm{allocationRule}(b, j) = \emptyset. $$ Equivalently, the allocation defines a (possibly partial) assignment of distinct items to distinct bidders.

Position in the library

These formats provide the outcome geometry: what bids look like and how allocations are encoded. They sit above the generic transfer-mechanism interface and below concrete mechanisms (Vickrey, first-price, VCG, Myerson, …) that fix allocation and payment rules. The single-parameter layer ([[mechanism_design.transfer.single_parameter_transfer_layer]]) is the scalar-allocation cousin used for Myerson-style theory; multi-item auctions naturally feed into the multi-parameter VCG analysis ([[mechanism_design.vcg.welfare_and_payments]]).

References

  • [Krishna, Chapters 2-3] Vijay Krishna, Auction Theory, 2nd ed., references/AuctionTheory.pdf. Standard sealed-bid auction formats and private-value auction models.
  • [Krishna, Chapter 11] Vijay Krishna, Auction Theory, 2nd ed., references/AuctionTheory.pdf. Multi-object auctions and bundle allocation.
  • [AGT, Chapter 1, Section 1.3.2] Nisan, Roughgarden, Tardos, and Vazirani, Algorithmic Game Theory, references/AlgorithmicGameTheory.pdf. First-price and second-price sealed-bid auctions as basic algorithmic game theory examples.
  • [AGT, Chapter 11] Nisan, Roughgarden, Tardos, and Vazirani, Algorithmic Game Theory, references/AlgorithmicGameTheory.pdf. Combinatorial auctions and feasibility constraints.

Provenance

lean_refs.name: SingleItemAuction
lean_refs.signature:
structure SingleItemAuction (I : Type*) (V : Type*) (P : Type*)
    extends MechanismWithTransfers I (fun _ => V) (Option I) P
/-- A multi-item auction with `k` distinct items.
  Agents report a bid vector (one value per item type). The mechanism allocates
  bundles of items: each agent receives a `Finset (Fin k)`.
  Feasibility (no item sold twice) is a separate predicate; see `IsFeasible`. -/

lean_refs.name: MultiItemAuction
lean_refs.signature:
structure MultiItemAuction (I : Type*) (k : ℕ) (V : Type*) (P : Type*)
    extends MechanismWithTransfers I (fun _ => Fin k → V) (I → Finset (Fin k)) P
namespace MultiItemAuction
/-- Feasibility: each item is allocated to at most one agent. -/

lean_refs.name: MultiItemAuction.IsFeasible
lean_refs.signature:
def IsFeasible {I : Type*} {k : ℕ} {V P : Type*}
    (M : MultiItemAuction I k V P) : Prop
lean_refs.docstring: Feasibility: each item is allocated to at most one agent.
